# Run coding agents

> The launchers, the model routing, and what this manual gives an agent.

Claude Code starts in the directory you are in and inherits the environment. The proxy lets you pick a model per session and tells you what quota is left. This manual is also the agent's brief — `help --json` hands it the same content as structured data, which is what stops it reaching for `grep` when `rg` is the tool here.

## `kern`

**Start Kern and its model service**

*shell*

Launch Kern normally. The machine hub owns routing, discovery, login state and recovery.

> **Why it is this way**
>
> Kern owns model access and recovery in one service.

See also: [`kern models`](./agents.md#kern-models) · [`kern models status`](./agents.md#kern-models-status)

## `cc [...args]`

**Start Claude in this directory**

*shell*

`cc` launches Claude Code with permission prompts skipped, in the directory you are in. Arguments pass straight through.

> **Why it is this way**
>
> With a single login profile it starts immediately — no picker. The multi-login machinery only wakes up once a second profile exists, so the common case pays nothing for it.

See also: [`cr [...args]`](./agents.md#resume-claude) · [`credentials in a capsule`](./containers.md#credentials-in-a-capsule)

## `kern launch claude`

**Launch a coding agent**

*shell*

The default model is auto:code. Use kern launch claude astra@chatgpt or kern launch codex auto:reasoning to select a model or frontier. Kern starts the service and attaches its MCP tools.

> **Why it is this way**
>
> Kern owns model access and recovery in one service.

See also: [`kern models`](./agents.md#kern-models) · [`kern models status`](./agents.md#kern-models-status)

## `cr [...args]` · `F4 s`

**Resume a Claude session in this directory**

Two routes to the same thing:

- `cr [...args]` *(shell)* — `cr` is `cc --resume`: it offers the sessions from this directory and continues the one you pick. Given an id it resumes that one without asking, which is the form `F4 s` types for you.
- `F4 s` *(terminal)* — In copy mode, reads back through this pane's scrollback for the newest `--resume` or `--continue` id, leaves the mode, and types `cr <id>` at the prompt WITHOUT running it — press Enter at the prompt, or edit the line first. Press the gesture again and it steps one id older, wrapping round to the newest; the status line says which of how many you are on. A pane that has never printed a session id says so and types nothing.

> **Why it is this way**
>
> `cr` on its own offers every session recorded for the directory, and they are uuids: the list cannot tell you which one is the session that just died in front of you. The scrollback can, because that session printed its own id there. So the pick is made from what this pane has seen rather than from what the directory holds, and the two routes stay side by side. The multiplexer can find the text without help — copy mode's search takes an extended regex — but it cannot KEEP the part that matched: a format hands over the whole cursor line and has no capture group, which is the one reason there is a script behind this key at all. Copy mode is left before anything is typed, because a pane sitting in a mode swallows sent keys and there is no route from inside the mode to the shell. The line is typed and not run: which session to resume is a decision, and the gesture stops one key short of making it. The cycle keeps its place in two pane options and resets when the NEWEST id in the pane changes — that is, exactly when a new session has announced itself. There is no timer and no hook to leave half-armed, which is what the widening `c` cycle retired on 2026-09-02 could not manage. It is `s` and not that freed `c` because a hand reaching for `c` in this mode is reaching to start a copy, whatever the table currently says.

See also: [`cc [...args]`](./agents.md#cc-args) · [`F4`](./copy.md#enter-copy-mode)

## Search with rg, find with fd, pick with tv

*shell*

Nothing to run — four rules that stop an agent guessing. Search with `rg` and find with `fd`, never `grep`/`find`. Pick with television (`tv`) — the single exception is `zi`, which opens fzf, and it is the only place fzf belongs. Nushell commands return structured data, so filter with `| where`, not `| grep`. And `cd` here can create the directory it is given.

> **Why it is this way**
>
> Every one of these is a failure this environment has actually seen: reaching for a tool that is not installed, or piping a table into a line-oriented filter and getting nothing.

See also: [`grep`](./files.md#grep) · [`tv channel`](./files.md#tv-channel) · [`cd <path>`](./directories.md#cd-path) · [`zi`](./directories.md#zi)

## `help --json`

**Read this manual as structured data**

*shell*

`help --json` emits the whole manual — topics and every entry field — as one JSON document, for an agent that would rather parse than read. Plain `help` under capture is already unstyled text, so this is the optimisation, not the requirement.

> **Why it is this way**
>
> The field names are an interface: renaming one is a breaking change and has to be recorded in the agent-interface PRD.

See also: [`help`](./maintaining.md#help) · [`idioms`](./agents.md#idioms)

## Understand how an agent comes up authenticated

*container*

Nothing to run: inside a capsule, `claude` and `opencode` both come up already authenticated, with no login prompt.

> **Why it is this way**
>
> The Claude and OpenCode tokens are exported from the host's login keychain into a read-only mount, then symlinked into place (`setup-credentials.sh:208-213`, `:224-229`) rather than copied. A writable copy would let the container run its own OAuth refresh, and Claude's refresh rotates the refresh token — so a capsule refreshing on its own would invalidate the host's login. Borrowing the host credential and failing closed is the trade: if the access token expires while a long-lived capsule sits idle, the agent asks to log in, and re-mounting (or running the agent on the host) heals it.

See also: [`capsule [dir]`](./containers.md#enter-capsule) · [`credentials in a capsule`](./containers.md#credentials-in-a-capsule) · [`cc [...args]`](./agents.md#cc-args)

## `<leader>x`

**Show what <leader>x can do**

*nvim normal*

Press `<leader>x` and pause: which-key lists the Claude maps — `c` toggle, `f` focus, `r` resume, `C` continue, `m` model, `b` add buffer, `s` send selection, `a` accept diff, `d` deny diff. Claude owns this prefix outright; nothing else sits on `x`.

See also: [`<leader>xc`](./agents.md#leader-xc)

## `<leader>xc`

**Toggle Claude**

*nvim normal*

Press `<leader>xc` to start Claude through `kern launch claude` in a pane using the coding frontier. Toggle again to hide or show it. From the Claude pane, `<C-j>` returns to the editor.

> **Why it is this way**
>
> Kern owns model selection, login state and recovery. The editor terminal provider preserves Claude IDE integration and tmux pane control.

See also: [`<leader>xf`](./agents.md#leader-xf) · [`kern launch claude`](./agents.md#kern-launch-claude) · [`cc [...args]`](./agents.md#cc-args)

## `<leader>xf`

**Focus Claude**

*nvim normal*

Press `<leader>xf` to jump into the Claude pane without toggling it — the move when it is already open and you want to type to it.

See also: [`<leader>xc`](./agents.md#leader-xc)

## `<leader>xr`

**Resume Claude**

*nvim normal*

Press `<leader>xr` to open the session picker for this directory inside the Claude pane and continue the one you pick — the in-editor twin of `cr` in the shell.

See also: [`<leader>xc`](./agents.md#leader-xc) · [`<leader>xC`](./agents.md#leader-xc) · [`cr [...args]`](./agents.md#resume-claude)

## `<leader>xC`

**Continue Claude**

*nvim normal*

Press `<leader>xC` to continue the most recent Claude conversation without a picker — where `<leader>xr` asks which one, this just resumes the latest.

See also: [`<leader>xr`](./agents.md#leader-xr)

## `<leader>xm`

**Select Claude model**

*nvim normal*

Press `<leader>xm` to pick the model the Claude pane runs on, without leaving the editor. That model choice lives in the pane's own profile, so it survives while the pane is open; the next fresh pane re-picks at spawn through `llm claude`. Native models are Claude Code's own, served by the Max plan.

See also: [`<leader>xc`](./agents.md#leader-xc) · [`kern launch claude`](./agents.md#kern-launch-claude)

## `<leader>xb`

**Add current buffer**

*nvim normal*

Press `<leader>xb` in a file buffer to hand that file to Claude as context, so the next prompt starts already knowing what you are looking at.

See also: [`<leader>xs`](./agents.md#leader-xs)

## `<leader>xs`

**Send to Claude**

*nvim visual*

Select text in visual mode and press `<leader>xs` to send exactly the selection to the Claude pane — the way to point at a snippet instead of describing it.

See also: [`<leader>xb`](./agents.md#leader-xb) · [`<leader>xc`](./agents.md#leader-xc)

## `<leader>xa`

**Accept diff**

*nvim normal*

Press `<leader>xa` to accept the inline diff Claude proposed for a buffer, keeping the change and closing the diff.

See also: [`<leader>xd`](./agents.md#leader-xd) · [`<leader>xc`](./agents.md#leader-xc)

## `<leader>xd`

**Deny diff**

*nvim normal*

Press `<leader>xd` to deny the inline diff Claude proposed, restoring the buffer as it was.

See also: [`<leader>xa`](./agents.md#leader-xa)
